amendments.rule: **A verbless clause with a prepositional predicate takes its supplied copula on the preposition.** Rule 20 supplies the copula from the construction; where the predicate is a prepositional phrase, the copula joins the preposition heading that phrase and the unit heads on the preposition — `בְּכַפֵּיהֶם` → *is in their hands*, `בִּמְסִלּוֹתָם` → *are in their paths*, `אִתָּנוּ` → *are with us*, `עָלֶיךָ` → *is upon thee*. **A resultative prepositional predicate takes the ASV's supplied result or change frame on the same terms.** The preposition carries the relation that English expresses with the frame: `לְ` → *to be*, *shall be turned into*, *will be unto*, or *shalt become*. This is not rule 20's wholly supplied lexical verb, because removing the English frame removes the preposition's own result relation; any explicit Hebrew subject still takes the English subject pronoun separately. Head the preposition's unit on the English word carrying that relation — *to* in *to be*, *into* in *shall be turned into*, *unto* in *will be unto*, and *become* where no English preposition remains. The ordinary copular case is settled rather than a tie: the corpus reads it this way in 103 units across 39 chapters and never moves the copula onto the object noun instead. It is settled; the note need not hedge it. **A relational verb the ASV writes where a copula would stand goes the same way.** Where a possessive or belonging `לְ` heads the predicate and the ASV renders the clause with a verb of belonging rather than a bare copula — `אֲשֶׁר לַבָּיִת` → *which belonged to the house* — that verb is part of the preposition's own rendering and joins its unit, headed on the English preposition written for it. It is not rule 20's wholly supplied lexical verb: drop the verb and the preposition's relation is what has gone and nothing else, which is the subtraction test rule 43 applies to the same clause written with *had*. Where the ASV does write *had* or *have*, rule 43 governs; where it writes a bare copula, the first sentence of this rule does.
amendments.why: Rule 49 speaks only of a copula and of a result or change frame, so a pass meeting `אֲשֶׁר לַבָּיִת` → *which belonged to the house* has rule 20's warning that a wholly supplied lexical verb is `added` on one side and nothing directly in point on the other. EZK.41.6 and 41.9 both put the verb on the preposition and head on *to*; the amendment records that and ties it to rule 43's subtraction test, which the corpus already backs with 72 `לְ` → *had* units, 23 *have* and 18 *hath*. No corpus row shown treats a belonging frame the other way, and the sentence is narrow enough not to disturb the settled copular case or rule 20's boundary.

conventions: Doubled סָבִיב סָבִיב, which the ASV renders once, is aligned on the first member of the pair and the second is unrepresented (rule 22), on rule 47's reasoning about a repeated article; a further lone סָבִיב standing on the other side of לַבַּיִת takes the second English expression the ASV writes. So 41.5's pair takes round about and its lone third takes on every side, while 41.10's lone first takes round about and the following pair takes on every side — the two look opposite in a lemma table and are one analysis, because the Hebrew orders differ. The same first-occurrence reading gives 41.23's coordinated possessive לְ its single had. BSB represents every occurrence, which is the whole Ncbsa column of disagreements and part of the Rd column.

מִפֹּה ... מִפֹּה is split under rule 2 into מִן → on and פֹּה → the one side / the other side, headed on one or other rather than on the generic side (rule 31); the ten units in 41.1, 41.2, 41.15, 41.19 and 41.26 all read this way. EZK.40 aligned the same two morphemes as one unit, on this side / on that side headed on on, where the ASV writes no article; that precedent was read and not followed here, because the ASV's the one side gives each morpheme English of its own and rule 30's one-English-rendering condition is unmet.

In the chapter's measurement clauses the numeral is the predicate and carries the construction-supplied copula — was five cubits, were three (rule 20) — while רֹחַב and אֹרֶךְ take only the word the ASV writes for them: the breadth, a breadth, broad, thick, long, The thickness. Where the ASV makes רֹחַב itself the predicate the copula goes there instead (41.1, which was the breadth of the tabernacle), and where the predicate is wholly elided in a gapped closing clause (41.20 thus was the wall, 41.26 thus were the side chambers) it falls back onto the explicit subject under rule 20's elided-predicate exception. The measure phrase's supplied of goes to the numeral, not to רֹחַב (41.8, 41.10).

לְ is read off the ASV in four ways here and they are not a split: unrendered before הַבַּיִת in the round about the house formula and for the second of two coordinated possessives (rule 40, 41.5/41.7/41.10/41.23); had or belonged to where the clause is possessive or a belonging relative (rules 43, 49); of where the ASV writes the relation itself (41.7 the breadth of the house); and its own directional word — for, toward, upon, by, on — elsewhere. In 41.7 the same לְמַעְלָה fuses whole to higher where the ASV writes one word and splits where it writes a supplied frame (went higher, continued upward), the frame going to the preposition under rule 49. The five Rd entries in the BSB column are this convention difference, not candidates.

report: Cross-verse consistency: no split found. All 51 candidate lemmas resolve to ASV-licensed differences. סָבִיב is uniform once the Hebrew order is read: an adjacent doubling is rendered once on the first member with the second unrepresented, and a further lone occurrence takes the second English expression — 41.5 (pair, then lone) and 41.10 (lone, then pair) look opposite in the table and are the same analysis. לְ divides four ways (unrendered, had/belonged to, of, directional word), each read off the ASV. הַ takes the, a determiner standing in the the's place (41.3 each, 41.5/41.18 every), or nothing, and every verse counts the ASV's the's against the article morphemes the same way (rules 29, 41, 47). אֶל, רֹחַב, אֹרֶךְ, פֹּה, פָּנֶה, פֶּתַח and the copula placements are all licensed by what the ASV writes.

One correction, in 41.21 only. Both supplied As for expressions were attached to the fronted nominals under rule 33; rule 16's third-family limit forecloses exactly that reading — הַהֵיכָל and וּפְנֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ carry no object marker and no fronting לְ, and rule 16 names rule 33 as unavailable for a topicalized nominal's fronting. Both are now their own added units headed on as. The verse pass had already named this as its competing reading, so the change applies a binding rule rather than re-weighing a tie.

BSB: none of the 23 disagreements is an error. The 10 Ncbsa are the doubled סָבִיב the ASV renders once (rule 22); the 5 Rd are לְ before הַבַּיִת in the round-about formula and the coordinated second possessive לְ of 41.23, on which the ASV spends no word (rule 40); the 6 Td are articles the ASV writes no the for (rules 29, 47). EZK.41.22's לוֹ is genuinely absent from the ASV text — that rendering stands only in the verse's margin — so both its morphemes stay unrepresented. No accepted edge was changed to move the rate.

One head a later reader may read the other way, left as accepted because it is a single occurrence with no cross-verse dimension: 41.16 נֶגֶד → over against heads on over, while 41.16 עַד → up to heads on to. Rule 31's subtraction can be read as putting נֶגֶד's head on against; the chapter's choice is recorded in the verse note.
Four conventions recorded (the log was empty against 58 repeating notes), and one amendment returned to rule 49 for the belonging frame belonged to. No corpus request was needed.
